assumptions: All figures are assumptions, not data from any real port.
Size: minimum is 1 terminal and 5 berths; reference is 8 terminals and 36 berths (Master_Context section 4). Berths are spread over terminals as evenly as possible.
Terminal types: reference has 5 CONTAINER and 3 NON_CONTAINER; minimum has 1 CONTAINER.
Berths: length uniform 180-400 m (container) or 150-300 m (non-container); max_vessel_loa is length minus 10 m; depth alongside uniform 11-16 m, datum LAT.

Arrivals: mean 26 requests a day at reference scale and 4 at minimum (26 x 5/36, rounded), plus integer noise in [-3, +3] with a floor of 1. ETAs are uniform within the day. The start date is fixed at 2026-01-05 00:00:00 UTC.

Vessels: one vessel per request. Types GENERAL_CARGO, CONTAINER, BULK_CARRIER and TANKER with weights 0.15, 0.55, 0.20 and 0.10 where a non-container terminal exists; minimum has container vessels only. LOA, beam ratio and max draft are drawn with triangular distributions inside per-type bounds. Arrival draft is 60-95% of max draft. Block coefficient is uniform 0.55-0.85. GT = 0.25 x LOA x beam x max draft; DWT = 1.4 x GT.

Per-type bounds (LOA in m as low-high with mode; beam as a share of LOA; max draft in m as low-high with mode): GENERAL_CARGO 90-200 mode 140, 0.15-0.18, 5-10 mode 7.5; CONTAINER 150-400 mode 300, 0.14-0.16, 8-16 mode 13; BULK_CARRIER 150-290 mode 220, 0.15-0.17, 9-17 mode 13; TANKER 120-250 mode 180, 0.15-0.17, 7-14 mode 10. Net tonnage = 0.6 x GT.
Vessel-to-berth fit is not guaranteed: a vessel's LOA or draft can exceed every berth or the channel depth. Feasibility tests must filter or expect that.
IMO numbers are random, unique seven-digit numbers whose check digit is deliberately wrong, so none can be a real ship.
Exact bytes depend on Python's random module (3.14 here); a Python upgrade can change them, and the samples are then regenerated from the register.
Requests: source EXTERNAL through one synthetic external system, status SUBMITTED. Container vessels request CONTAINER terminals; other vessels request NON_CONTAINER ones.
Tugboats: 12 at reference scale, 3 at minimum; 40-80 tonnes bollard pull, all AVAILABLE.
One navigation channel (depth 16 m, width 250 m, 10 knots, datum LAT) with 4 waypoints.
The port is at latitude 0, longitude 0 with no UN/LOCODE. Time zone is Africa/Cairo.
Not generated: users, tides, weather, pilots, tug masters, containers, BAPLIE data, recommendations. The schema copy is docs/ref/db/schema.sql (PortHub b4d2deb).
